title: Fylgja twin.json v4 — the twin’s record (M2 FR-012; M5 FR-022; M10 FR-013; M11 FR-026–FR-028)
description: Written by the record step into the twin directory after every node is ready; removed with the directory by unstage. Carries the manifest's provenance block (never observed_at from the bundle: D-023), observed_at when the run performed a read and an explicit statement that it is unknown when it did not (Constitution VI), the bundle_id, the provisioning run's identity, and the version of the binary that provisioned it. Nothing here is a credential. M5: twin_version is 2, and each node records the artifact it was pushed — name, content type, checksum and size, copied from the staged manifest — and how long its push took. Never the artifact’s bytes (FR-028). Everything else is v1’s, with M4’s meaning. M7: unchanged (FR-026: no new key); twin_version stays 2. M10: twin_version is 3, and the record names the waypoint the twin was created from — series, sequence, description and the at’s source — or null when it was created with --branch or from a bundle; provenance.at carries the at itself. Nothing else is new. A waypoint is only ever recorded on a pinned, intent-sourced record. M11: twin_version is 4. The record gains state (ready or diverged), a step block (the last step: outcome, the side it came from and the side it went to or towards, the step run, the phase that failed, containerlab's plan with each touched node's declared and reported link-change behaviour, every push with its outcome, the readiness and push timings, when it started and ended, and the failure's findings) or null for a twin that has not stepped, and nodes[].holds, the bundle_id whose bootstrap and artifact the node is last known to run, or null for a node containerlab restarted, recreated or created that no push landed on, which runs its baseline alone (R7.6). After a stepped or unchanged step bundle_id, provenance, observed_at and waypoint are the target's; after a diverged step they stay the previous record's and step.to names the target. run stays the create's. A create writes a 4 record with state ready, step null and holds equal to bundle_id on every node. The record is written whole on every path after the step's stage. No device diff, no artifact or bootstrap line, no credential.

lab.description: The fixed containerlab lab name (Constitution VII).

bundle_id.description: Identity of the staged bundle (D-024); equals the store entry it was copied from.

provenance.description: Copied verbatim from the staged manifest's provenance block.

at.description: Present iff the operator supplied --at; verbatim.

observed_at.description: UTC start of the read that produced this twin's CTM (six fractional digits, as the CTM envelope), when the run performed a read; null when it did not, in which case observed_at_note says so.

observed_at_note.description: Required when observed_at is null: the explicit statement that the read time is unknown and why (provisioned from an existing bundle; no read took place). Absent otherwise.

source.description: intent: created by `twin create` (read + compile in the run). bundle: provisioned by `twin provision` from an existing bundle.

run.description: The provisioning run's identity in Temporal (D-007).

provisioned_by.description: The worker binary that provisioned the twin. Identifies the binary and reaches no bundle (D-024).

recorded_at.description: UTC time the record was written, from the worker's clock. Informational.

nodes.description: One entry per node, sorted by name, as containerlab reported them at deploy and as readiness observed them. M11 (FR-027, FR-028): after a step, the nodes are containerlab's report after the reconcile; after a reconcile that failed or was cut short, the lab as clab inspect reports it when the record is written (a created node present, a deleted one gone), or the inspection taken before the stage when that read fails; when no reconcile ran, the inspection taken before the stage. Each node's ready_after_s and pushed_in_s are the step's where the step awaited or pushed it, and the previous record's otherwise.

mgmt_ipv4.description: The management address containerlab assigned, without prefix length (R1: ipv4_address is reported as 172.20.20.2/24).

ready_after_s.description: Seconds from the readiness step's start for this node to the probe's first success. M11: after a step, the step's own readiness (step.ready_after) for a node the step awaited; the previous record's value for every other node, or 0 for a created node it lacks.

artifact.description: The artifact pushed to this node: the manifest entry minus its file path. Name and checksum are what twin show, the dry run and every finding name an artifact by (FR-027). M11: the artifact of the bundle holds names.

pushed_in_s.description: Seconds from the push activity’s start for this node to the node’s commit. M11: after a step, the step's own time (step.pushed[].took_s) for a node whose push landed; 0 for a node that holds null, which runs its baseline alone; the previous record's value for every other node, a node whose push was refused, failed or not attempted included.

holds.description: M11 (FR-028): the bundle_id whose bootstrap and artifact this node is last known to run: the record's bundle_id on a create and on every node a stepped step pushed or left as it was. After a diverged step: the target's on a node whose push landed; null for a node containerlab restarted, recreated or created whose push did not land, which runs containerlab's baseline alone; the previous bundle's on every other node. null and the previous are what the node last ran that the step knows of, not a claim that a push which did not land left it untouched: a push whose step.pushed[].outcome is failed may have committed (a replace that darkens a node, FR-019), and only refused is the node's own atomic answer. A later rollback reads step.pushed[].outcome beside holds (FR-014). artifact is the artifact of the bundle holds names (the previous record's entry beside a null).

waypoint.description: M10 (FR-013): the waypoint the CLI resolved and passed to the record step as data (wire.RecordInput.Waypoint), or null. The at is provenance.at; at_source says whether it was written on the waypoint (given) or is the waypoint's own write time (written).

state.description: ready: the twin is at the record's waypoint and bundle. diverged: the last step failed or was cancelled after the host was touched; the twin is up, step says where it stopped, and it accepts only fylgja twin destroy (M11 FR-014).

step.description: M11 (FR-027): the last step, or null for a twin that has not stepped. A step is one twin step: from the bundle the record named to one waypoint of the same series.

waypoint.description: M10 (FR-013): the waypoint the CLI resolved and passed to the record step as data (wire.RecordInput.Waypoint), or null. The at is provenance.at; at_source says whether it was written on the waypoint (given) or is the waypoint's own write time (written).

at.description: the side’s pinned at, verbatim (the waypoint’s resolved at)

waypoint.description: M10 (FR-013): the waypoint the CLI resolved and passed to the record step as data (wire.RecordInput.Waypoint), or null. The at is provenance.at; at_source says whether it was written on the waypoint (given) or is the waypoint's own write time (written).

at.description: the side’s pinned at, verbatim (the waypoint’s resolved at)

phase.description: the phase that failed; null unless outcome is diverged

reconcile.description: containerlab's plan (clab deploy --dry-run --format json, R9.1) with each touched node's package declaration beside what containerlab reported, and the apply's time; skipped true with no took_s when the plan was empty (its lists empty) or the step was unchanged, whose run applies nothing (its lists still containerlab's plan as read)

declared.description: the node's package's fidelity.link_change; null when the node is created (no package declaration applies)

reason.description: containerlab's node-change-reasons text, when it gave one

took_s.description: the apply, from clab deploy’s start to its return; absent when skipped

outcome.description: landed: the node committed the replace. refused: the node's own answer; a refused replace is atomic, so the node runs what it ran before (R7.2, R7.3). failed: no answer settled the push (the node did not answer within push_timeout_s, the heartbeat was lost, or the cancellation reached it, rule run.cancelled), and it may have committed: a replace that darkens a node commits and then times out on every attempt (FR-019). not_attempted: an earlier phase failed. A later rollback reads this beside nodes[].holds, the bundle last known to run on the node (FR-014).

rule.description: the finding’s identifier for a refused or failed push

timings.description: a phase not reached is absent

ended_at.description: RFC 3339 UTC, workflow.Now() at the record; the pause at a waypoint is this to the next step’s started_at (FR-030)

findings.description: the failure’s findings for a diverged step; [] otherwise; never content
